name: Botox versus solifenacin
question: In solifenacin-naïve adults with refractory overactive bladder and urinary incontinence, how do onabotulinumtoxinA and solifenacin compare with placebo?

design.population: Solifenacin-naïve adults with overactive bladder and urinary incontinence after inadequate response to or intolerance of an anticholinergic.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy phase 3b randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Study Participants and Study Design, p 168; Figure 1, p 169

verdictNote: Both co-primary outcomes favored each active treatment versus placebo; comparisons were unadjusted for multiplicity.
takeaway: In solifenacin-naïve patients with refractory overactive bladder, onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U and solifenacin 5–10 mg reduced daily urinary incontinence and increased complete continence versus placebo at 12 weeks; the onabotulinumtoxinA–solifenacin comparison was post hoc.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Herschorn S, Kohan A, Aliotta P, et al. "The Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA or Solifenacin Compared with Placebo in Solifenacin Naïve Patients with Refractory Overactive Bladder: Results from a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind Phase 3b Trial." *J Urol.* 2017;198(1):167-175. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2017.01.069
reports.followUp: Week 12 primary assessment; later open-label onabotulinumtoxinA treatment 2
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Design, p 168; Outcomes, p 170

results.measure: Least squares mean change in daily urinary incontinence episodes from baseline to treatment-1 week 12 (ITT)

effect.p: <0.001 for each active arm versus placebo

results.note: Both active arms met their placebo comparison; comparisons were not adjusted for multiplicity. Direct onabotulinumtoxinA versus solifenacin analysis was post hoc. Numerical between-arm confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 169; Outcomes and Figure 2A, pp 170–171

results.measure: 100% reduction in daily urinary incontinence episodes at treatment-1 week 12 (ITT)
results.note: The displayed numerators follow from the rounded percentages and ITT arm sizes in Figure 3A; comparisons were not adjusted for multiplicity.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 169; Outcomes, p 170; Figure 3A, p 172

results.measure: Post hoc comparison of least squares mean change in daily episodes at treatment-1 week 12 (ITT)
results.note: Post hoc direct comparison favored onabotulinumtoxinA.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 169; Outcomes, p 170; Figure 2A, p 171

results.measure: Least squares mean change in daily micturitions from baseline to treatment-1 week 12 (ITT)
results.locator: Full text, Other Overactive Bladder Symptoms and Table 2, pp 171–173

results.measure: 100% reduction in daily urinary incontinence episodes 12 weeks after treatment 2 among week-12 evaluable recipients, by original randomization arm
results.note: All received open-label onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U; denominators are the week-12 evaluable subset shown in Figure 3B, not all randomized patients.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, pp 170–171; Figure 3B, p 172

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 171; Table 3, p 173
harms.note: Treatment cycle 1 (24 weeks), safety population. UTI required bacteriuria and leukocyturia regardless of symptoms.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: Full text, Efficacy and Safety Evaluations, p 169; Safety, p 171; Table 3, p 173
harms.note: Treatment cycle 1 (24 weeks), safety population. Retention was PVR at least 350 mL regardless of symptoms or 200–349 mL with symptoms requiring CIC per investigator.

harms.label: Symptomatic urinary tract infection
harms.note: Treatment cycle 1, safety population; numerators are calculated from reported percentages and arm denominators.

harms.label: Clean intermittent catheterization
harms.note: Treatment cycle 1, safety population; numerators are calculated from reported percentages and arm denominators.

delivery.label: Double-dummy initial treatment
delivery.value: Day-1 detrusor injection of onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U in 10 mL or saline placebo, avoiding the trigone, with daily solifenacin or placebo capsule; solifenacin started at 5 mg and could increase to 10 mg at week 6 (48/151 randomized patients, 31.8%, escalated).
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Design, p 168; Patient Demographic and Baseline Characteristics, p 169

delivery.label: Open-label second treatment
delivery.value: At weeks 12, 18 or 24, eligible patients could request open-label onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U after at least 12 weeks since injection, at least 2 UUI episodes/day, at most 1 UI-free day in a 3-day diary and PVR below 200 mL; 213/356 (59.8%) received treatment 2 (78/145, 90/151 and 45/60 by original arm).
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Design, p 168; Figure 1, p 169; Patient Demographic and Baseline Characteristics, p 170
